test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 02 Sept, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A trader claims to sell flour at a profit of 58%, but also dishonestly uses a weight which is 8% less than what is mentioned on it. Find the total percentage of profit earned by the trader. (Round off the answer to the nearest whole number.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive approach: **Profit** of 58% means ratio of 100 : 158.

**Dishonest weight** of 8% less means trader gives 92 units instead of 100.

The effective **ratio** is (100 × 92) : (158 × 100) ⇒ 92 : 158.

**Total Profit %** = (158 − 92) ÷ 92 × 100 = 66 ÷ 92 × 100.

Total Profit % ≈ 0.71739 × 100 = 71.739% ≈ 72%.

**∴ The correct answer is 72%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Profit claim = 58%, Weight error = 8% less.

**Formulas:** Overall Profit % = [(Actual SP − Actual CP) ÷ Actual CP] × 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/22cda5ee92160405adad0f5dc5593863775ef78dd27a0bc743dddff724ef0897.png] 

⇒ Let the **True Weight** be 1000g and **Cost Price (CP)** be Rs. 1 per gram.

⇒ Trader sells it as 1000g but charges for 58% profit: **Selling Price (SP)** = 1000 × 1.58 = Rs. 1580.

⇒ The **Actual weight** given is 8% less than 1000g: 1000 − (8% of 1000) = 920g.

⇒ The **Actual CP** for the trader is the cost of 920g = Rs. 920.

⇒ **Total Profit** = 1580 − 920 = Rs. 660.

⇒ **Profit %** = (660 ÷ 920) × 100 = 71.739...% ≈ 72%.

**∴ The correct answer is 72%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer uses less weight, the **Profit %** = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100. If there is an additional markup, we combine the effects.

Rounding Off

If the decimal part is **0.5 or higher**, round up to the next **whole number**; if less than 0.5, stay at the current integer.</p
